title: A closed subset of a spectral space is spectral
statement: Let $X$ be a spectral space [def-weil-spectral-space] and $E\subseteq X$ a closed subset. Then $E$ with the induced topology is a spectral space; moreover its quasi-compact open subsets are exactly the sets $E\cap U$ with $U\subseteq X$ quasi-compact open.

source.place: Topology, Lemma (Tag 0902, label lemma-spectral-sub, line 4428), case of a closed subset (closed sets are closed in the constructible topology); used in literature/stacks-project/etale-cohomology.tex, proof of Lemma 59.82.1 (Tag 09ZG, line 15155)

proof.text: $E$ is sober. The space $X$ is sober [def-weil-spectral-space] and $E$ is closed in $X$, so $E$ with the induced topology is sober by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subspace-sober]. (Stacks argues for $E$ closed in the constructible topology: for $Z\subseteq E$ irreducible closed with generic point $\eta$ of its closure $\overline Z$ in $X$ one shows $\eta\in E$. When $E$ is closed in $X$, $Z$ is closed in $X$, so $\overline Z=Z$ and $\eta\in Z\subseteq E$ directly; this is the closed case of Tag 0B31.)

source.place: Topology, Lemma (Tag 0902, label lemma-spectral-sub, line 4428), proof, first paragraph (sobriety), specialized to $E$ closed

proof.text: $E$ is quasi-compact. $X$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-spectral-space] and $E$ is closed, so $E$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact]. (Stacks uses that $E$ is closed in the constructible topology, Tags 005C and 0901; for $E$ closed in $X$ Tag 005C applied to $X$ itself suffices.)

source.place: Topology, Lemma (Tag 0902, label lemma-spectral-sub, line 4428), proof, second paragraph, first two sentences, specialized to $E$ closed

proof.text: For every quasi-compact open $U\subseteq X$, the set $E\cap U$ is a quasi-compact open subset of $E$. It is open in $E$ by definition of the induced topology. The space $U$ (induced topology) is quasi-compact and $E\cap U$ is closed in $U$, being the trace of the closed set $E$; so $E\cap U$ is quasi-compact in the topology induced from $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact]. That topology equals the one induced from $E$, both being induced from $X$, so $E\cap U$ is a quasi-compact open of $E$.

source.place: Topology, Lemma (Tag 0902, label lemma-spectral-sub, line 4428), proof, second paragraph, sentence 'If $U\subset X$ is a quasi-compact open, then $E\cap U$ is ... quasi-compact', specialized to $E$ closed

proof.text: Every quasi-compact open $V\subseteq E$ is of the form $E\cap U$ with $U\subseteq X$ quasi-compact open. Write $V=E\cap W$ with $W\subseteq X$ open. Since the quasi-compact opens of $X$ form a basis [def-weil-spectral-space], $W=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ with $U_i$ quasi-compact open, so $V=\bigcup_i(E\cap U_i)$ is a covering of $V$ by opens of $E$. As $V$ is quasi-compact, $V=(E\cap U_{i_1})\cup\dots\cup(E\cap U_{i_n})=E\cap U$ with $U=U_{i_1}\cup\dots\cup U_{i_n}$, which is open and quasi-compact as a finite union of quasi-compact subsets (a covering of $U$ by opens restricts to a covering of each $U_{i_k}$; take the union of the finite subcoverings). Together with the previous step, the quasi-compact opens of $E$ are exactly the sets $E\cap U$ with $U\subseteq X$ quasi-compact open. (Stacks states this as 'It follows that'; the inclusion written out here is left implicit there.)

source.place: Topology, Lemma (Tag 0902, label lemma-spectral-sub, line 4428), proof, second paragraph, sentence 'It follows that the quasi-compact open subsets of $E$ are the intersections $E\cap U$'

proof.text: The quasi-compact opens of $E$ form a basis of its topology. Let $V\subseteq E$ be open and $x\in V$; write $V=E\cap W$ with $W\subseteq X$ open. By the basis property of $X$ [def-weil-spectral-space] there is a quasi-compact open $U$ with $x\in U\subseteq W$; then $x\in E\cap U\subseteq V$, and $E\cap U$ is quasi-compact open in $E$ by the third step.

source.place: Topology, Lemma (Tag 0902, label lemma-spectral-sub, line 4428), proof, second paragraph, 'These form a basis for the topology'

proof.text: $E$ is quasi-separated. Let $V,V'\subseteq E$ be quasi-compact open. By the fourth step $V=E\cap U$, $V'=E\cap U'$ with $U,U'\subseteq X$ quasi-compact open, so $V\cap V'=E\cap(U\cap U')$; $U\cap U'$ is quasi-compact open as $X$ is quasi-separated [def-weil-spectral-space], hence $V\cap V'$ is quasi-compact by the third step.

source.place: Topology, Lemma (Tag 0902, label lemma-spectral-sub, line 4428), proof, last sentences ('given two $U,U'\subset X$ quasi-compact opens, the intersection $(E\cap U)\cap(E\cap U')=E\cap(U\cap U')$ ...')

proof.text: Conclusion. By the first, second, fifth and sixth steps $E$ is sober, quasi-compact, quasi-separated and its quasi-compact opens form a basis, i.e. $E$ is spectral [def-weil-spectral-space]; the description of its quasi-compact opens is the third and fourth steps.

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against Stacks Topology Lemma 0902 (lemma-spectral-sub, topology.tex line 4428; tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags) in the case of a closed subset; statement kept, it is correct and self-contained. Wrote the proof in seven steps following the Stacks proof specialized to E closed: sobriety and quasi-compactness of E become the closed cases of Tags 0B31 and 005C, which are two new Mathlib leaves (lem-weil-pbc-closed-subspace-sober: Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.quasiSober + Subtype.t0Space; lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact: IsClosed.isCompact), so neither the constructible topology (Tag 0901) nor Tag 005K is needed. The remaining steps (traces of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact open; conversely every quasi-compact open of E is such a trace, which Stacks leaves implicit and is written out here; basis; quasi-separatedness) use only def-weil-spectral-space and the leaf 005C. The item is not itself a Mathlib leaf: Mathlib has the closed-embedding results for QuasiSober, PrespectralSpace (PrespectralSpace.of_isClosedEmbedding), CompactSpace and T0, but no QuasiSeparatedSpace for a closed subspace and no SpectralSpace for a closed subspace (only Topology.IsOpenEmbedding.spectralSpace); no Lean candidate in the slopmaster2 sources.
